egypt/mountains.caption: Sinai
egypt/mountains.description: Mount Sinai and Saint Catherine's, and granite peaks over two thousand metres above the Red Sea.
egypt/mountains.alt: the granite peaks of the Sinai above Saint Catherine's, Egypt

egypt/nature.caption: The Nile and the Desert
egypt/nature.description: A green ribbon a few kilometres wide, and sand for a thousand kilometres either side of it.
egypt/nature.alt: the green Nile valley meeting desert on both banks, Egypt

egypt/outdoor.caption: Dive, Sail, Ride
egypt/outdoor.description: Reef diving at Marsa Alam, feluccas at Aswan, and camels in the Western Desert.
egypt/outdoor.alt: divers entering the water on the Red Sea coast, Egypt

egypt/photography.caption: The Light at Six
egypt/photography.description: Desert light at either end of the day is the whole reason to be up early here.
egypt/photography.alt: dawn light on the temple columns at Luxor, Egypt

egypt/safari.caption: The Western Desert
egypt/safari.description: Not big game — desert fox, gazelle and the silence of the Great Sand Sea.
egypt/safari.alt: the White Desert chalk formations at dusk, Egypt

egypt/traditional-people.caption: Nubians and Bedouin
egypt/traditional-people.description: Nubian villages above Aswan and Bedouin communities in the Sinai and the Western Desert.
egypt/traditional-people.alt: a brightly painted Nubian village on the Nile at Aswan, Egypt

egypt/waterfalls.caption: The First Cataract
egypt/waterfalls.description: The Nile's cataracts at Aswan — rapids rather than falls, and the reason the boats stopped here.
egypt/waterfalls.alt: the Nile running over granite at the Aswan cataract, Egypt

egypt/why-visit.caption: The Oldest Journey
egypt/why-visit.description: People have been travelling to see this country for two and a half thousand years.
egypt/why-visit.alt: the Sphinx and the Great Pyramid at sunrise, Egypt

egypt/wildlife.caption: Birds of the Delta
egypt/wildlife.description: Two million migrating birds use the Delta and the Red Sea coast as a flyway each year.
egypt/wildlife.alt: flamingos and waders on a Nile delta wetland, Egypt

ethiopia/adventure.caption: Trekking Country
ethiopia/adventure.description: Multi-day treks in the Simiens and Bale, and the Danakil at a hundred metres below sea level.
ethiopia/adventure.alt: the sulphur springs of the Danakil depression, Ethiopia

ethiopia/architecture.caption: Round Houses and Rock Churches
ethiopia/architecture.description: The tukul, and the rock architecture of Tigray cut into cliff faces you have to climb.
ethiopia/architecture.alt: a Tigray rock church high in a cliff face, Ethiopia

ethiopia/beaches.caption: No Coast, and No Loss
ethiopia/beaches.description: Landlocked since 1993 — the water here is the Rift lakes and the crater lakes of Bishoftu.
ethiopia/beaches.alt: a crater lake at Bishoftu in the early morning, Ethiopia

ethiopia/cities.caption: Addis Ababa
ethiopia/cities.description: Founded 1886, at 2,355 metres, and the diplomatic capital of the continent.
ethiopia/cities.alt: the Merkato district of Addis Ababa from above, Ethiopia

ethiopia/crafts.caption: Weaving and Silver
ethiopia/crafts.description: Handwoven shemma cotton, and Coptic crosses in silver, each region with its own shape.
ethiopia/crafts.alt: a silversmith working an Ethiopian cross

ethiopia/culture.caption: Its Own Everything
ethiopia/culture.description: Its own alphabet, its own calendar with thirteen months, and its own church since the fourth century.
ethiopia/culture.alt: priests in white robes outside a rock-hewn church, Ethiopia

ethiopia/eco-tourism.caption: Community Conservation
ethiopia/eco-tourism.description: Guides and scouts drawn from the villages inside the parks, which is why the wolves are still there.
ethiopia/eco-tourism.alt: a park scout looking out over the Bale plateau, Ethiopia

ethiopia/family-community.caption: Highland Travel
ethiopia/family-community.description: Cool highland air, short flights between the historic sites, and no malaria at altitude.
ethiopia/family-community.alt: a family walking a highland track in northern Ethiopia

ethiopia/festivals.caption: Timkat and Meskel
ethiopia/festivals.description: Timkat in January at Gondar, and Meskel bonfires across the country in September.
ethiopia/festivals.alt: the Timkat procession with white-robed crowds at Gondar, Ethiopia

ethiopia/food.caption: Injera and Doro Wat
ethiopia/food.description: Sourdough injera under everything, and fasting food that has made vegans of visitors.
ethiopia/food.alt: injera with several wats served on a shared platter, Ethiopia

ethiopia/forests.caption: Harenna and the Church Forests
ethiopia/forests.description: Harenna's cloud forest in Bale, and the church forests that are the last woodland of the north.
ethiopia/forests.alt: a round church surrounded by its own remnant forest, Ethiopia

ethiopia/heritage.caption: Aksum and Gondar
ethiopia/heritage.description: The Aksumite stelae, and the seventeenth-century castles of Gondar built by Fasilides.
ethiopia/heritage.alt: the stone castles of Fasil Ghebbi at Gondar, Ethiopia

ethiopia/hero.caption: The Roof of Africa
ethiopia/hero.description: Eighty per cent of Africa's land above three thousand metres is in this one country.
ethiopia/hero.alt: the Simien mountains escarpment dropping away into cloud, Ethiopia

ethiopia/hidden-gems.caption: Tigray
ethiopia/hidden-gems.description: Rock churches in cliff faces reached by hand and foot, with almost nobody else there.
ethiopia/hidden-gems.alt: the climb to a rock church in the Gheralta mountains, Ethiopia

ethiopia/historic-sites.caption: Lalibela
ethiopia/historic-sites.description: Eleven churches cut down into solid rock in the twelfth century, still in use every day.
ethiopia/historic-sites.alt: the rock-hewn church of Bete Giyorgis at Lalibela, Ethiopia

ethiopia/lakes-rivers.caption: Lake Tana
ethiopia/lakes-rivers.description: The source of the Blue Nile, with monasteries on its islands still in use.
ethiopia/lakes-rivers.alt: an island monastery on Lake Tana seen from the water, Ethiopia

ethiopia/local-life.caption: Coffee, Properly
ethiopia/local-life.description: Coffee was found here, and it is still roasted, ground and poured in front of you.
ethiopia/local-life.alt: a coffee ceremony with roasting pan and jebena, Ethiopia

ethiopia/luxury.caption: Lodges on the Escarpment
ethiopia/luxury.description: Limalimo and Bale Mountain Lodge — small, sited well, and built by people who stayed.
ethiopia/luxury.alt: a lodge terrace on the edge of the Simien escarpment, Ethiopia

ethiopia/mountains.caption: The Simiens
ethiopia/mountains.description: Ras Dashen is 4,550 metres; the trek to it runs along the escarpment for days.
ethiopia/mountains.alt: trekkers on the ridge trail in the Simien mountains, Ethiopia

ethiopia/nature.caption: Escarpment and Rift
ethiopia/nature.description: The Rift Valley cuts the whole country in half, with highlands either side of it.
ethiopia/nature.alt: the Ethiopian Rift valley lakes seen from the escarpment

ethiopia/outdoor.caption: Trek and Climb
ethiopia/outdoor.description: The Simien traverse, Bale's plateau, and the Tigray churches that need a rope.
ethiopia/outdoor.alt: a climber on the approach to a Tigray cliff church, Ethiopia

ethiopia/photography.caption: Faces and Escarpments
ethiopia/photography.description: The light at four thousand metres, and portraiture that has to be asked for properly.
ethiopia/photography.alt: cloud below the escarpment edge in the Simien mountains, Ethiopia

ethiopia/safari.caption: Bale and the Ethiopian Wolf
ethiopia/safari.description: The Bale mountains hold the last five hundred Ethiopian wolves, on the Sanetti plateau.
ethiopia/safari.alt: an Ethiopian wolf on the Sanetti plateau in Bale

ethiopia/traditional-people.caption: Omo Valley
ethiopia/traditional-people.description: The lower Omo holds sixteen peoples in one valley, and the visits should be arranged carefully.
ethiopia/traditional-people.alt: a village of the lower Omo valley at the end of the day, Ethiopia

ethiopia/waterfalls.caption: The Blue Nile Falls
ethiopia/waterfalls.description: Tis Issat — the water that smokes — where the Blue Nile leaves Lake Tana.
ethiopia/waterfalls.alt: the Blue Nile falls in full flow at Tis Issat, Ethiopia

ethiopia/why-visit.caption: Nothing Else Like It
ethiopia/why-visit.description: No colonial period, its own script, its own calendar, and its own year that starts in September.
ethiopia/why-visit.alt: a priest holding a processional cross at a rock church, Ethiopia

ethiopia/wildlife.caption: Gelada and Walia Ibex
ethiopia/wildlife.description: The gelada lives nowhere else on earth, and grazes the Simien escarpment in troops of hundreds.
ethiopia/wildlife.alt: a troop of gelada baboons grazing on the Simien escarpment, Ethiopia

ghana/adventure.caption: Canopy, Surf and Lake
ghana/adventure.description: The Kakum walkway, Busua's beach breaks, and hiking the Volta hills to the Togo border.
ghana/adventure.alt: a hiking trail through the hills of the Volta region, Ghana

ghana/architecture.caption: Posuban and Colonial Coast
ghana/architecture.description: The Fante posuban shrines, and the trading architecture strung along the coast road.
ghana/architecture.alt: a painted Fante posuban shrine in a coastal town, Ghana

ghana/beaches.caption: Busua and Cape Three Points
ghana/beaches.description: Surf at Busua, and the point where the country runs out into the Gulf of Guinea.
ghana/beaches.alt: palms above the beach at Busua on the Ghanaian coast

ghana/cities.caption: Accra and Kumasi
ghana/cities.description: Accra on the Atlantic, and Kumasi's Kejetia — one of the largest markets in West Africa.
ghana/cities.alt: the vast Kejetia market spread out at Kumasi, Ghana

ghana/crafts.caption: Kente and Adinkra
ghana/crafts.description: Kente woven in strips at Bonwire, and adinkra symbols stamped by hand at Ntonso.
ghana/crafts.alt: adinkra symbols being stamped onto cloth by hand, Ghana

ghana/culture.caption: Ashanti
ghana/culture.description: A kingdom that fought the British to a standstill, and still keeps its own court at Kumasi.
ghana/culture.alt: the Manhyia palace grounds at Kumasi, Ghana

ghana/eco-tourism.caption: Community Forest
ghana/eco-tourism.description: The Wechiau hippo sanctuary and the Boabeng-Fiema monkey sanctuary, both village-run.
ghana/eco-tourism.alt: hippos in the Black Volta at the Wechiau sanctuary, Ghana

ghana/family-community.caption: Easy First Africa
ghana/family-community.description: English-speaking, short distances, and about as gentle an introduction as the continent offers.
ghana/family-community.alt: children playing on a beach on the Ghanaian coast

ghana/festivals.caption: Homowo and Chale Wote
ghana/festivals.description: Homowo in Accra in August, and the Chale Wote street art festival in Jamestown.
ghana/festivals.alt: a street art festival crowd in Jamestown, Accra, Ghana

ghana/food.caption: Jollof, Banku and Grilled Tilapia
ghana/food.description: The jollof argument is unwinnable; the tilapia off the grill with banku settles it.
ghana/food.alt: grilled tilapia and banku served at a roadside chop bar, Ghana

ghana/forests.caption: Kakum
ghana/forests.description: Rainforest with a canopy walkway thirty metres up, strung between seven emergent trees.
ghana/forests.alt: the canopy walkway suspended above Kakum rainforest, Ghana

ghana/heritage.caption: The Year of Return
ghana/heritage.description: Ghana asked the diaspora to come back, and a great many people did.
ghana/heritage.alt: a memorial gathering at Cape Coast castle, Ghana

ghana/hero.caption: The Forts, the Forest and the Highlife
ghana/hero.description: Coastal forts, Ashanti gold, elephants in the north, and a band playing somewhere every night.
ghana/hero.alt: the white walls of Cape Coast castle above the Atlantic, Ghana

ghana/hidden-gems.caption: Nzulezo
ghana/hidden-gems.description: A village built entirely on stilts over Lake Tandane, reached only by canoe.
ghana/hidden-gems.alt: the stilt village of Nzulezo over the water, Ghana

ghana/historic-sites.caption: The Slave Forts
ghana/historic-sites.description: Cape Coast and Elmina — the doors of no return, kept as they were and not softened.
ghana/historic-sites.alt: the door of no return at Elmina castle, Ghana

ghana/lakes-rivers.caption: Lake Volta
ghana/lakes-rivers.description: The largest reservoir on earth by surface area, with ferries that take a full day to cross it.
ghana/lakes-rivers.alt: fishing boats on Lake Volta at first light, Ghana

ghana/local-life.caption: Chop Bars and Trotros
ghana/local-life.description: The country runs on shared minibuses and roadside kitchens, and both are worth using.
ghana/local-life.alt: a busy trotro station in Accra, Ghana

ghana/luxury.caption: Lodges on the Water
ghana/luxury.description: Small lodges above the beach at Busua and Axim, and the Mole escarpment rooms over the waterhole.
ghana/luxury.alt: a lodge terrace overlooking the waterhole at Mole, Ghana

ghana/mountains.caption: The Akwapim and Afadja
ghana/mountains.description: Afadjato is 885 metres and the highest point, walkable in a morning from Liati Wote.
ghana/mountains.alt: the green hills of the Volta region from Afadjato, Ghana

ghana/nature.caption: Coast to Savanna
ghana/nature.description: Rainforest and lagoon in the south, transitional woodland through the middle, savanna at Mole.
ghana/nature.alt: rainforest canopy in Kakum national park, Ghana

ghana/outdoor.caption: Surf, Hike, Paddle
ghana/outdoor.description: Busua's breaks, the Volta hills, and canoes on the lake at Dodi.
ghana/outdoor.alt: a surfer walking out at Busua beach, Ghana

ghana/photography.caption: Colour Everywhere
ghana/photography.description: Kente, market cloth and painted trotros — nothing here is any colour by accident.
ghana/photography.alt: stacked bolts of printed cloth in a Ghanaian market

ghana/safari.caption: Walking Safari at Mole
ghana/safari.description: One of the few parks in West Africa where the game drive is done on foot, with an armed ranger.
ghana/safari.alt: a ranger leading walkers through savanna at Mole, Ghana

ghana/traditional-people.caption: The Ewe and the Dagomba
ghana/traditional-people.description: Kente weaving in Volta and Ashanti, and the Dagbon drumming traditions of the north.
ghana/traditional-people.alt: a weaver working a kente loom in Bonwire, Ghana

ghana/waterfalls.caption: Wli
ghana/waterfalls.description: The highest falls in West Africa, dropping out of forest on the Togo border, with bats overhead.
ghana/waterfalls.alt: the Wli waterfall dropping through forest in the Volta region, Ghana

ghana/why-visit.caption: The Gentle Introduction
ghana/why-visit.description: English, good roads, a short flight from Europe, and everything within a day's drive.
ghana/why-visit.alt: a coastal road running along the Gulf of Guinea, Ghana

ghana/wildlife.caption: Mole and Ankasa
ghana/wildlife.description: Elephants that walk into the camp waterhole at Mole, and forest elephants at Ankasa.
ghana/wildlife.alt: elephants at the waterhole below Mole motel, Ghana

kenya/adventure.caption: Balloon Over the Mara
kenya/adventure.description: Up before dawn, an hour over the plains at treetop height, and breakfast on the grass where you land.
kenya/adventure.alt: a hot-air balloon over the Maasai Mara plains at sunrise, Kenya

reasons: looks like 56% of a slot already filled here

kenya/architecture.caption: Coral Stone and Carved Doors
kenya/architecture.description: Swahili coral-rag houses with inner courtyards, and doors carved in Lamu and shipped up the coast.
kenya/architecture.alt: an ornately carved Swahili door in a coral stone wall in Lamu, Kenya

kenya/beaches.caption: The Swahili Coast
kenya/beaches.description: Diani, Watamu and Lamu: white sand, warm Indian Ocean, and a coastline that traded with Arabia for a thousand years.
kenya/beaches.alt: white sand and dhows on Diani Beach on the Indian Ocean, Kenya

kenya/cities.caption: Nairobi, Green City in the Sun
kenya/cities.description: The only capital on earth with a national park inside the city limits, and lions in sight of the skyline.
kenya/cities.alt: the Nairobi skyline seen across Nairobi National Park, Kenya

kenya/crafts.caption: Beadwork and Kisii Stone
kenya/crafts.description: Maasai beadwork, Kisii soapstone carving, and kiondo sisal baskets made the way they always were.
kenya/crafts.alt: Maasai women stringing beadwork ornaments, Kenya

kenya/culture.caption: Maasai and Swahili
kenya/culture.description: Two Kenyas: the cattle-keeping highlands and the coral-stone, Arabic-inflected coast.
kenya/culture.alt: Maasai elders in red shuka cloth on the open plains, Kenya

kenya/eco-tourism.caption: Rhino, Counted Daily
kenya/eco-tourism.description: Ol Pejeta and Lewa run some of Africa's most closely monitored rhino populations, funded by the beds on the property.
kenya/eco-tourism.alt: black rhino grazing on the Ol Pejeta conservancy at dawn, Kenya

kenya/family-community.caption: The Conservancies
kenya/family-community.description: Community conservancies lease grazing land back for wildlife, and the lease pays the schools around the Mara.
kenya/family-community.alt: a community conservancy ranger team on patrol near the Maasai Mara, Kenya

kenya/festivals.caption: Lamu Cultural Festival
kenya/festivals.description: Dhow races, donkey races, henna and taarab music in the alleys of a town with almost no cars.
kenya/festivals.alt: dhow racing during the Lamu cultural festival, Kenya

kenya/food.caption: Nyama Choma and Ugali
kenya/food.description: Goat roasted over charcoal, maize meal, sukuma wiki, and coastal biryani that came in by dhow.
kenya/food.alt: nyama choma roasting over charcoal at a Nairobi grill, Kenya

kenya/forests.caption: Kakamega, the Last of It
kenya/forests.description: The only Kenyan remnant of the Guineo-Congolian rainforest that once ran clear across the continent.
kenya/forests.alt: dense canopy and hanging vines inside Kakamega Forest, Kenya

kenya/heritage.caption: Lamu Old Town
kenya/heritage.description: The oldest continuously inhabited Swahili settlement, carved doors, coral rag walls and no room for a car.
kenya/heritage.alt: carved wooden doors and coral stone alleys in Lamu Old Town, Kenya

kenya/hero.caption: Where the Safari Was Invented
kenya/hero.description: The Maasai Mara at first light, and everything the word safari has meant for a century.
kenya/hero.alt: acacia and open grassland in the Maasai Mara at sunrise, Kenya

kenya/hidden-gems.caption: Chalbi and Marsabit
kenya/hidden-gems.description: The desert north: Chalbi's salt pan, Marsabit's forested crater and the road down to Lake Turkana.
kenya/hidden-gems.alt: the salt pan and dunes of the Chalbi desert in northern Kenya

kenya/historic-sites.caption: Fort Jesus, Mombasa
kenya/historic-sites.description: Portuguese, built 1593, taken and retaken nine times — now UNESCO World Heritage above the old harbour.
kenya/historic-sites.alt: the coral ramparts of Fort Jesus above Mombasa old harbour, Kenya

kenya/lakes-rivers.caption: Flamingo Country
kenya/lakes-rivers.description: Nakuru, Bogoria and Elementaita hold soda water, hot springs and flamingo in numbers that change by the season.
kenya/lakes-rivers.alt: flamingos massed on the shallows of Lake Nakuru, Kenya

kenya/local-life.caption: Matatus and Markets
kenya/local-life.description: Painted, over-amplified matatus, Maasai Market on rotation through the week, and tea at every stop.
kenya/local-life.alt: brightly painted matatu minibuses in a Nairobi street, Kenya

kenya/luxury.caption: Camps on the Mara
kenya/luxury.description: Small tented camps on private conservancies, night drives and off-road access the main reserve does not allow.
kenya/luxury.alt: a luxury tented safari camp overlooking the Maasai Mara plains, Kenya

kenya/mountains.caption: Mount Kenya, 5,199 m
kenya/mountains.description: Equatorial glaciers, giant lobelia, and a trekking route to Point Lenana that needs no technical climbing.
kenya/mountains.alt: the jagged glaciated peaks of Mount Kenya above the moorland

kenya/nature.caption: The Great Rift Valley
kenya/nature.description: The escarpment drops away below the Naivasha road, holding a chain of soda lakes and dormant volcanoes.
kenya/nature.alt: the Great Rift Valley escarpment and floor seen from the Naivasha road, Kenya

kenya/outdoor.caption: Walking Hell's Gate
kenya/outdoor.description: The one Kenyan park you can walk and cycle through, with gorge scrambling and geothermal steam.
kenya/outdoor.alt: cyclists on the track between the cliffs of Hell's Gate National Park, Kenya

kenya/photography.caption: Kilimanjaro from Amboseli
kenya/photography.description: The mountain is in Tanzania; the view of it is in Kenya, and it is only clear for an hour at each end of the day.
kenya/photography.alt: elephants beneath Mount Kilimanjaro seen from Amboseli at sunrise, Kenya

kenya/safari.caption: The Great Migration
kenya/safari.description: Between July and October a million wildebeest cross the Mara river, and the crocodiles are already waiting.
kenya/safari.alt: wildebeest crossing the Mara river during the great migration, Kenya

kenya/traditional-people.caption: Samburu and Maasai
kenya/traditional-people.description: Samburu in the northern drylands, Maasai in the south, both still moving cattle between seasonal grazing.
kenya/traditional-people.alt: a Samburu warrior with beaded ornaments in the northern drylands, Kenya

kenya/waterfalls.caption: Thomson's Falls
kenya/waterfalls.description: The Ewaso Ng'iro drops seventy-four metres into a fern gorge at Nyahururu, on the way north to Samburu.
kenya/waterfalls.alt: Thomson's Falls dropping into the fern gorge at Nyahururu, Kenya

kenya/why-visit.caption: Magical Kenya
kenya/why-visit.description: Migration, glacier, reef and desert inside one border, with the infrastructure to see all four in a fortnight.
kenya/why-visit.alt: acacia silhouetted against a red sunset on the Kenyan savannah

kenya/wildlife.caption: Wildlife on the Savannah
kenya/wildlife.description: The Big Five, plus the reticulated giraffe and Grevy's zebra that live nowhere south of here.
kenya/wildlife.alt: elephants crossing the plain at Amboseli beneath Kilimanjaro, Kenya

madagascar/adventure.caption: The RN7 and the Tsingy
madagascar/adventure.description: The road south through the highlands, and the limestone tsingy you cross on via ferrata.
madagascar/adventure.alt: a walker crossing the tsingy on a rope bridge, Madagascar

madagascar/architecture.caption: Highland Brick
madagascar/architecture.description: Two-storey red brick with a wooden balcony, and nothing else in Africa looks like it.
madagascar/architecture.alt: red brick highland houses with wooden balconies, Madagascar

madagascar/beaches.caption: Nosy Be and the East Coast
madagascar/beaches.description: Reef, whale sharks and humpbacks off Nosy Be, and long empty sand on the east coast.
madagascar/beaches.alt: a white sand beach and turquoise water at Nosy Be, Madagascar

madagascar/cities.caption: Antananarivo
madagascar/cities.description: A capital built up twelve hills, with stairs instead of streets in half of it.
madagascar/cities.alt: the stepped hillside houses of Antananarivo, Madagascar

madagascar/crafts.caption: Silk, Raffia and Zafimaniry
madagascar/crafts.description: Wild silk lambas, raffia work, and the Zafimaniry woodcarving of the south-east.
madagascar/crafts.alt: a woman weaving a silk lamba on a wooden loom, Madagascar

madagascar/culture.caption: Malagasy, and Eighteen Peoples
madagascar/culture.description: One language across the island, of Austronesian origin, and eighteen distinct peoples speaking it.
madagascar/culture.alt: a highland Malagasy village of red brick houses, Madagascar

madagascar/eco-tourism.caption: The Reason to Come Carefully
madagascar/eco-tourism.description: Deforestation is the country's crisis, and the parks that work are the ones the villages run.
madagascar/eco-tourism.alt: a reforestation nursery beside a Madagascar rainforest park

madagascar/family-community.caption: Slow, and Worth It
madagascar/family-community.description: Roads are slow and distances are long — but the children will hold a chameleon.
madagascar/family-community.alt: children on a village path in rural Madagascar

madagascar/festivals.caption: Hira Gasy and Donia
madagascar/festivals.description: Hira gasy troupes in the highlands, and the Donia festival on Nosy Be in June.
madagascar/festivals.alt: a hira gasy troupe performing in the highlands, Madagascar

madagascar/food.caption: Romazava and Rice
madagascar/food.description: Rice three times a day, and romazava — beef and greens — with it.
madagascar/food.alt: romazava and rice served at a Malagasy table, Madagascar

madagascar/forests.caption: Rainforest and Spiny Forest
madagascar/forests.description: Andasibe and Ranomafana in the east, and the spiny forest of the south which is like nowhere.
madagascar/forests.alt: the spiny forest of octopus trees in southern Madagascar

madagascar/heritage.caption: Pirates and Kingdoms
madagascar/heritage.description: Île Sainte-Marie's pirate cemetery, and the Merina kingdom that unified the island.
madagascar/heritage.alt: the pirate cemetery on Île Sainte-Marie, Madagascar

madagascar/hero.caption: An Island That Evolved Alone
madagascar/hero.description: Ninety per cent of what lives here lives nowhere else, because it has been on its own since the dinosaurs.
madagascar/hero.alt: the avenue of baobabs at Morondava at sunset, Madagascar

madagascar/hidden-gems.caption: Masoala
madagascar/hidden-gems.description: The largest protected rainforest in the country, reached by boat, with whales in the bay.
madagascar/hidden-gems.alt: the rainforest of Masoala coming down to the sea, Madagascar

madagascar/historic-sites.caption: The Rova and the Royal Hills
madagascar/historic-sites.description: Ambohimanga, the royal hill of the Merina kings above Antananarivo.
madagascar/historic-sites.alt: the wooden royal compound at Ambohimanga, Madagascar

madagascar/lakes-rivers.caption: The Tsiribihina
madagascar/lakes-rivers.description: Three days downriver by pirogue through country with no road in it.
madagascar/lakes-rivers.alt: a pirogue on the Tsiribihina river at dawn, Madagascar

madagascar/local-life.caption: The Zebu Market
madagascar/local-life.description: Zebu cattle are wealth here, and the markets that trade them are the real calendar.
madagascar/local-life.alt: a zebu cattle market in the Madagascar highlands

madagascar/luxury.caption: Small Lodges
madagascar/luxury.description: Owner-run lodges at the park gates, and beach places on Nosy Be with a dozen rooms.
madagascar/luxury.alt: a small lodge among trees at a Madagascar park gate

madagascar/mountains.caption: The Highlands and Maromokotro
madagascar/mountains.description: The central highlands run to two thousand metres; Maromokotro reaches 2,876 in the Tsaratanana.
madagascar/mountains.alt: terraced rice paddies in the Madagascar highlands

madagascar/nature.caption: Six Ecosystems on One Island
madagascar/nature.description: Rainforest east, highlands centre, spiny forest south, dry deciduous west, and reef all round.
madagascar/nature.alt: the tsingy limestone pinnacles of Bemaraha, Madagascar

madagascar/outdoor.caption: Trek, Paddle, Dive
madagascar/outdoor.description: Rainforest trekking, the Tsiribihina by pirogue, and reef diving off Nosy Be.
madagascar/outdoor.alt: kayaks on the water off a Madagascar reef island

madagascar/photography.caption: Baobabs at Six
madagascar/photography.description: The avenue at Morondava for twenty minutes at either end of the day, and nothing else like it.
madagascar/photography.alt: baobabs silhouetted against the sky at Morondava, Madagascar

madagascar/safari.caption: Not a Safari Island
madagascar/safari.description: No lions and no elephant — the wildlife here is small, nocturnal, and worth the torchlight.
madagascar/safari.alt: a chameleon on a branch in Ranomafana rainforest, Madagascar

madagascar/traditional-people.caption: Famadihana and the Ancestors
madagascar/traditional-people.description: The ancestors are present here in a way that shapes the calendar and the architecture.
madagascar/traditional-people.alt: a family tomb standing in highland Madagascar farmland

madagascar/waterfalls.caption: The Eastern Escarpment
madagascar/waterfalls.description: Short, steep rivers off the escarpment, and waterfalls through the rainforest at Andasibe.
madagascar/waterfalls.alt: a waterfall in rainforest on the eastern escarpment, Madagascar

madagascar/why-visit.caption: Nowhere Else
madagascar/why-visit.description: Lemurs, baobabs, tsingy, spiny forest — none of it exists anywhere else on earth.
madagascar/why-visit.alt: a ring-tailed lemur troop in southern Madagascar

madagascar/wildlife.caption: A Hundred Kinds of Lemur
madagascar/wildlife.description: A hundred and seven species and subspecies of lemur, every one of them endemic.
madagascar/wildlife.alt: an indri lemur in the rainforest canopy at Andasibe, Madagascar

mauritius/adventure.caption: Kite, Dive, Hike
mauritius/adventure.description: Kitesurfing at Le Morne, diving the outer reef, and hiking the gorges and the mountains.
mauritius/adventure.alt: kitesurfers on the lagoon below Le Morne, Mauritius

mauritius/architecture.caption: Colonial and Estate
mauritius/architecture.description: The plantation houses of the interior, and the colonial buildings of Port Louis.
mauritius/architecture.alt: a colonial plantation house with a wide veranda, Mauritius

mauritius/beaches.caption: The Lagoon
mauritius/beaches.description: Inside the reef the water is flat and warm the whole way round the island.
mauritius/beaches.alt: turquoise lagoon and reef break off a Mauritian beach, Mauritius

mauritius/cities.caption: Port Louis
mauritius/cities.description: A working port and capital, with a market, a waterfront and the Champ de Mars.
mauritius/cities.alt: the Port Louis waterfront and market, Mauritius

mauritius/crafts.caption: Model Ships and Textiles
mauritius/crafts.description: Model shipbuilding, and a textile industry that grew out of the sugar estates.
mauritius/crafts.alt: a model ship being built in a Mauritian workshop, Mauritius

mauritius/culture.caption: Four Continents
mauritius/culture.description: Indian, African, French and Chinese, in one Creole language and one calendar.
mauritius/culture.alt: a Hindu temple and a church on the same Mauritian street, Mauritius

mauritius/eco-tourism.caption: Bringing Back the Birds
mauritius/eco-tourism.description: The kestrel, the pink pigeon and the echo parakeet were each brought back from near zero.
mauritius/eco-tourism.alt: a pink pigeon in Mauritian native forest, Mauritius

mauritius/family-community.caption: Made for Families
mauritius/family-community.description: Flat warm lagoon, no dangerous surf inside the reef, and short drives from anywhere.
mauritius/family-community.alt: children playing in a calm Mauritian lagoon, Mauritius

mauritius/festivals.caption: Maha Shivaratri and Cavadee
mauritius/festivals.description: Half a million walking to Grand Bassin in February, and Thaipoosam Cavadee in January.
mauritius/festivals.alt: pilgrims walking to Grand Bassin at Maha Shivaratri, Mauritius

mauritius/food.caption: Dholl Puri and Rougaille
mauritius/food.description: Dholl puri off a street cart, rougaille at home, and a fish vindaye that is entirely local.
mauritius/food.alt: dholl puri being made at a street cart, Mauritius

mauritius/forests.caption: Black River Gorges
mauritius/forests.description: The last of the native forest, on the plateau, with trails and endemic birds in it.
mauritius/forests.alt: native forest in the Black River Gorges, Mauritius

mauritius/hero.caption: Reef, Sugar and the Volcanic Interior
mauritius/hero.description: A ring of reef, a green interior of sugar and mountain, and four cultures on one island.
mauritius/hero.alt: the mountain of Le Morne rising above the lagoon, Mauritius

mauritius/hidden-gems.caption: Rodrigues
mauritius/hidden-gems.description: Six hundred kilometres east, a tenth the size, and the island Mauritius used to be.
mauritius/hidden-gems.alt: the hills and lagoon of Rodrigues island, Mauritius

mauritius/historic-sites.caption: Aapravasi Ghat
mauritius/historic-sites.description: The immigration depot where half a million indentured labourers first landed.
mauritius/historic-sites.alt: the stone steps of the Aapravasi Ghat, Mauritius

mauritius/lakes-rivers.caption: Grand Bassin
mauritius/lakes-rivers.description: A crater lake and Hindu pilgrimage site, with half a million people walking to it at Maha Shivaratri.
mauritius/lakes-rivers.alt: the temple and statues at Grand Bassin crater lake, Mauritius

mauritius/local-life.caption: The Central Market
mauritius/local-life.description: Port Louis market in the morning, for vegetables, tea and alouda.
mauritius/local-life.alt: the vegetable stalls of Port Louis central market, Mauritius

mauritius/luxury.caption: The Resort Standard
mauritius/luxury.description: The island effectively invented the Indian Ocean resort, and it still does it best.
mauritius/luxury.alt: a resort beach and lagoon in the late afternoon, Mauritius

mauritius/mountains.caption: Le Morne and Pieter Both
mauritius/mountains.description: Le Morne Brabant stands 556 metres out of the lagoon, and is walked in a morning.
mauritius/mountains.alt: the summit ridge of Le Morne Brabant above the sea, Mauritius

mauritius/nature.caption: Lagoon and Gorge
mauritius/nature.description: Lagoon all the way round, sugar cane across the plain, and gorges cut into the plateau.
mauritius/nature.alt: the Black River gorges in morning cloud, Mauritius

mauritius/outdoor.caption: Kite, Hike, Dive
mauritius/outdoor.description: Le Morne's kite lagoon, the Black River trails, and dive sites outside the reef.
mauritius/outdoor.alt: hikers on the trail up Le Morne, Mauritius

mauritius/photography.caption: Lagoon Colour
mauritius/photography.description: The lagoon changes colour every hundred metres, and the aerial work here is the proof.
mauritius/photography.alt: aerial view of a Mauritian lagoon and reef, Mauritius

mauritius/safari.caption: Reef, Not Savanna
mauritius/safari.description: No big game — the wildlife here is the reef, the endemic birds, and the flying foxes at dusk.
mauritius/safari.alt: fruit bats leaving a roost at dusk, Mauritius

mauritius/traditional-people.caption: Creole and Bhojpuri
mauritius/traditional-people.description: Creole spoken by everyone, Bhojpuri in the villages, and French and English in print.
mauritius/traditional-people.alt: a village street in the Mauritian sugar country, Mauritius

mauritius/waterfalls.caption: Chamarel
mauritius/waterfalls.description: A hundred metres in a single drop, near the seven-coloured earths.
mauritius/waterfalls.alt: the Chamarel waterfall dropping into forest, Mauritius

mauritius/why-visit.caption: Four Cultures, One Lagoon
mauritius/why-visit.description: A Hindu festival, a Creole kitchen, a French road name and a Chinese shop, in one street.
mauritius/why-visit.alt: a busy multicultural street scene in Port Louis, Mauritius

mauritius/wildlife.caption: What the Dodo Left
mauritius/wildlife.description: The dodo is gone, but the pink pigeon and the kestrel were both brought back from single figures.
mauritius/wildlife.alt: a Mauritius kestrel perched in native forest

morocco/adventure.caption: Dunes, Gorges and Surf
morocco/adventure.description: Trekking in the Atlas, surfing the Atlantic points, and a night out on the erg at Chegaga.
morocco/adventure.alt: a trekking trail high on a ridge in the High Atlas, Morocco

morocco/architecture.caption: Riad and Medina
morocco/architecture.description: Rooms built inward around a courtyard, because the street was never meant to see in.
morocco/architecture.alt: the tiled courtyard of a traditional Moroccan riad, Morocco

morocco/beaches.caption: The Atlantic Coast
morocco/beaches.description: Essaouira's wind, Taghazout's point breaks, and the long empty beaches between them.
morocco/beaches.alt: the walled seafront of Essaouira with fishing boats, Morocco

morocco/cities.caption: Marrakesh and Casablanca
morocco/cities.description: Jemaa el-Fnaa at dusk, and the Atlantic modernism of Casablanca an hour up the road.
morocco/cities.alt: Jemaa el-Fnaa square in Marrakesh filling at dusk, Morocco

morocco/crafts.caption: Zellige, Leather and Wool
morocco/crafts.description: Tile cut by hand in Fez, tanned leather, and carpets woven to patterns held in memory.
morocco/crafts.alt: a craftsman cutting zellige tile by hand in Fez, Morocco

morocco/culture.caption: Amazigh and Arab
morocco/culture.description: Three Amazigh languages, Arabic, French and Spanish, and a culture that predates all of them.
morocco/culture.alt: an Amazigh village of earth houses built into a hillside, Morocco

morocco/eco-tourism.caption: Oasis Agriculture
morocco/eco-tourism.description: The khettara irrigation channels still working, and the argan cooperatives run by women.
morocco/eco-tourism.alt: a palm oasis irrigated by traditional channels, Morocco

morocco/family-community.caption: Easy Travelling
morocco/family-community.description: Short drives, good roads, and a train line down the coast that children enjoy.
morocco/family-community.alt: a family walking a quiet lane in a Moroccan hill village, Morocco

morocco/festivals.caption: Moussem and Gnaoua
morocco/festivals.description: The Gnaoua festival in Essaouira in June, and the moussems that mark the harvest.
morocco/festivals.alt: musicians playing at the Gnaoua festival in Essaouira, Morocco

morocco/food.caption: Tagine, Bread and Mint
morocco/food.description: Slow-cooked tagine, bread baked in the neighbourhood oven, and tea poured from height.
morocco/food.alt: a tagine cooking over charcoal at a roadside stall, Morocco

morocco/forests.caption: The Cedar Forest
morocco/forests.description: The Middle Atlas cedar, some of it a thousand years old, above Ifrane and Azrou.
morocco/forests.alt: ancient Atlas cedar trees in the Middle Atlas forest, Morocco

morocco/heritage.caption: The Imperial Cities
morocco/heritage.description: Fez, Marrakesh, Meknes and Rabat — four capitals, each of a different dynasty.
morocco/heritage.alt: the tanneries and rooftops of the Fez medina, Morocco

morocco/hero.caption: Where the Atlas Meets the Sahara
morocco/hero.description: Snow on the High Atlas in the morning and the first dunes of the Sahara by evening.
morocco/hero.alt: the High Atlas mountains rising behind a Moroccan kasbah, Morocco

morocco/hidden-gems.caption: Chefchaouen and the Rif
morocco/hidden-gems.description: The blue town in the Rif, and a mountain range most itineraries drive straight past.
morocco/hidden-gems.alt: the blue-painted lanes of Chefchaouen in the Rif, Morocco

morocco/historic-sites.caption: Volubilis and the Kasbahs
morocco/historic-sites.description: A Roman city on the plain at Volubilis, and Ait Benhaddou standing above the Ounila.
morocco/historic-sites.alt: the earth kasbah of Ait Benhaddou above the river, Morocco

morocco/lakes-rivers.caption: The Draa River
morocco/lakes-rivers.description: The longest river in Morocco, mostly dry, and green the whole way where it is not.
morocco/lakes-rivers.alt: palm groves along the Draa valley in southern Morocco

morocco/local-life.caption: The Souk in the Morning
morocco/local-life.description: Before the tour groups, the medina is simply where people buy their vegetables.
morocco/local-life.alt: a produce market in a Moroccan medina early in the morning, Morocco

morocco/luxury.caption: Desert Camps and Riads
morocco/luxury.description: Erg Chigaga camps well beyond the day-trip dunes, and riads restored room by room.
morocco/luxury.alt: a desert camp of tents on the dunes at Erg Chigaga, Morocco

morocco/mountains.caption: The High Atlas
morocco/mountains.description: Toubkal is 4,167 metres and the highest point in North Africa, walkable in two days from Imlil.
morocco/mountains.alt: Mount Toubkal under snow above the village of Imlil, Morocco

morocco/nature.caption: The Draa and the Dades
morocco/nature.description: Palm oases strung along the Draa, and gorges cut red through the Dades and the Todra.
morocco/nature.alt: the Todra gorge with red rock walls and a river below, Morocco

morocco/outdoor.caption: Trek, Surf, Ride
morocco/outdoor.description: Multi-day Atlas treks, Atlantic surf schools, and horses on the Essaouira sand.
morocco/outdoor.alt: surfers walking the beach at Taghazout at sunset, Morocco

morocco/photography.caption: Light on Earth Walls
morocco/photography.description: Pisé takes late light the way nothing else does, which is why every photographer comes here.
morocco/photography.alt: late light on the earth walls of a southern Moroccan kasbah, Morocco

morocco/safari.caption: Desert Country
morocco/safari.description: Not the safari of the east — the wildlife here is desert-adapted, and you look for it at first light.
morocco/safari.alt: a desert track through stony hammada in southern Morocco

morocco/traditional-people.caption: The People of the Atlas
morocco/traditional-people.description: Village life at two thousand metres, where the year is still organised around the snow.
morocco/traditional-people.alt: a shepherd with his flock on a High Atlas terrace, Morocco

morocco/waterfalls.caption: Ouzoud
morocco/waterfalls.description: A hundred metres of water in three stages, with macaques in the olive trees beside it.
morocco/waterfalls.alt: the Ouzoud falls dropping in stages through olive trees, Morocco

morocco/why-visit.caption: Two Days, Four Climates
morocco/why-visit.description: Surf in the morning, cedar forest by lunch, and the Sahara the following evening.
morocco/why-visit.alt: a road climbing a High Atlas pass with the Sahara beyond, Morocco

morocco/wildlife.caption: Barbary Macaques and the Argan Forest
morocco/wildlife.description: Macaques in the cedar forest above Azrou, and goats standing in the argan trees near Essaouira.
morocco/wildlife.alt: Barbary macaques in the cedar forest of the Middle Atlas, Morocco

mozambique/adventure.caption: Dive, Sail, Kayak
mozambique/adventure.description: Manta and whale shark at Tofo, dhow safaris in the Quirimbas, and kayaks in the mangrove.
mozambique/adventure.alt: a diver with a manta ray off Tofo, Mozambique

mozambique/architecture.caption: Coral Stone and Colonial
mozambique/architecture.description: Coral rag on the islands, and Portuguese modernism through Maputo and Beira.
mozambique/architecture.alt: a colonial-era building in Maputo with modernist lines, Mozambique

mozambique/beaches.caption: Bazaruto and the Quirimbas
mozambique/beaches.description: Dune islands in the south, coral islands in the north, and dhows between them.
mozambique/beaches.alt: the sand dunes and turquoise water of Bazaruto, Mozambique

mozambique/cities.caption: Maputo
mozambique/cities.description: Wide avenues, a Mediterranean seafront, and the market Eiffel's company built.
mozambique/cities.alt: the Maputo waterfront and the Indian Ocean, Mozambique

mozambique/crafts.caption: Carving and Basketry
mozambique/crafts.description: Makonde blackwood carving, and the palm basketry of the northern islands.
mozambique/crafts.alt: Makonde blackwood carvings on a workshop bench, Mozambique

mozambique/culture.caption: Portuguese and Swahili
mozambique/culture.description: Five hundred years of Portuguese on a Swahili coast, and a culture made from both.
mozambique/culture.alt: the coral-stone lanes of Ilha de Moçambique, Mozambique

mozambique/eco-tourism.caption: Gorongosa's Restoration
mozambique/eco-tourism.description: Local employment, local science, and a park brought back from nothing — worth understanding.
mozambique/eco-tourism.alt: a park scientist at work in Gorongosa, Mozambique

mozambique/family-community.caption: Warm Water All Year
mozambique/family-community.description: Shallow, warm and calm inside the reef — as easy a sea as the continent offers.
mozambique/family-community.alt: children swimming in shallow water inside a reef, Mozambique

mozambique/festivals.caption: Marrabenta and Timbila
mozambique/festivals.description: Marrabenta on the coast, and the Chopi timbila orchestras of Inhambane.
mozambique/festivals.alt: a Chopi timbila orchestra performing, Mozambique

mozambique/food.caption: Peri-Peri and Matapa
mozambique/food.description: Prawns with peri-peri, and matapa — cassava leaf and coconut — with rice.
mozambique/food.alt: grilled prawns with peri-peri at a beach kitchen, Mozambique

mozambique/forests.caption: Coastal Forest
mozambique/forests.description: The coastal dry forest of the north, and the mangrove that lines most of the delta.
mozambique/forests.alt: mangrove forest along a northern Mozambique estuary

mozambique/heritage.caption: The Swahili Coast
mozambique/heritage.description: Ibo, Angoche and Sofala — Indian Ocean trading towns older than the Portuguese.
mozambique/heritage.alt: the crumbling colonial buildings of Ibo island, Mozambique

mozambique/hero.caption: Two Thousand Kilometres of Coast
mozambique/hero.description: Reef, dune and island for the whole length of the country, and warm water all year.
mozambique/hero.alt: a dhow sailing off a Mozambican island at sunrise, Mozambique

mozambique/hidden-gems.caption: Ibo Island
mozambique/hidden-gems.description: Silversmiths, a fort, mangrove channels, and about as far from a resort as it gets.
mozambique/hidden-gems.alt: a silversmith working inside the fort on Ibo island, Mozambique

mozambique/historic-sites.caption: Ilha de Moçambique
mozambique/historic-sites.description: The old capital, on a coral island a kilometre long, with a fort at one end.
mozambique/historic-sites.alt: the fortress of São Sebastião on Ilha de Moçambique, Mozambique

mozambique/lakes-rivers.caption: The Zambezi and Cahora Bassa
mozambique/lakes-rivers.description: The Zambezi's last five hundred kilometres, and the Cahora Bassa lake above them.
mozambique/lakes-rivers.alt: the Zambezi river wide in the Mozambican lowlands, Mozambique

mozambique/local-life.caption: The Beach Market
mozambique/local-life.description: Fish landed and sold on the sand, and the dhow that brought it still on the beach.
mozambique/local-life.alt: fish being sold on the sand beside a dhow, Mozambique

mozambique/luxury.caption: Island Lodges
mozambique/luxury.description: A handful of very good island lodges in Bazaruto and the Quirimbas, and little else on them.
mozambique/luxury.alt: an island lodge among palms above a white beach, Mozambique

mozambique/mountains.caption: Mount Namuli and Gorongosa
mozambique/mountains.description: Namuli at 2,419 metres, and Gorongosa's own mountain with rainforest on top of it.
mozambique/mountains.alt: the granite dome of Mount Namuli rising from farmland, Mozambique

mozambique/nature.caption: Reef and Miombo
mozambique/nature.description: Coral reef the whole coast, miombo woodland inland, and the Rift's southern end at Gorongosa.
mozambique/nature.alt: the Gorongosa floodplain in the green season, Mozambique

mozambique/outdoor.caption: Dive and Sail
mozambique/outdoor.description: Whale shark season at Tofo, dhow safaris in the Quirimbas, and reef diving throughout.
mozambique/outdoor.alt: a dhow under sail between coral islands, Mozambique

mozambique/photography.caption: Dhow Light
mozambique/photography.description: Lateen sails at either end of the day, and water that photographs as three colours at once.
mozambique/photography.alt: dhows silhouetted against a Mozambican sunrise, Mozambique

mozambique/safari.caption: Niassa and Gorongosa
mozambique/safari.description: Niassa is one of the largest reserves in Africa, and among the least visited anywhere.
mozambique/safari.alt: a game track through Niassa reserve woodland, Mozambique

mozambique/traditional-people.caption: Makonde and Makua
mozambique/traditional-people.description: Makonde carving in the north, and the Makua women's mussiro face paint.
mozambique/traditional-people.alt: a Makonde carver at work in northern Mozambique

mozambique/waterfalls.caption: Murchison of the South
mozambique/waterfalls.description: Waterfalls off the Zambezi escarpment, and the Lugenda's rapids in the far north.
mozambique/waterfalls.alt: a waterfall off the escarpment in northern Mozambique

mozambique/why-visit.caption: The Coast Nobody Has Ruined Yet
mozambique/why-visit.description: Two thousand kilometres of Indian Ocean, and most of it still without a road to it.
mozambique/why-visit.alt: an empty Indian Ocean beach with palms behind it, Mozambique

mozambique/wildlife.caption: Gorongosa
mozambique/wildlife.description: A park that lost almost everything in the war and has spent twenty years getting it back.
mozambique/wildlife.alt: waterbuck on the Gorongosa floodplain, Mozambique

namibia/hero.caption: Where the Desert Meets the Wild
namibia/hero.description: The oldest desert on earth running straight into the Atlantic, and almost nobody on it.
namibia/hero.alt: red dunes at Sossusvlei with long morning shadows, Namibia

namibia/nature.caption: The Namib
namibia/nature.description: Fifty-five million years old, and dunes at Sossusvlei three hundred metres high.
namibia/nature.alt: the dune field of the Namib at first light, Namibia

namibia/safari.caption: Etosha
namibia/safari.description: Game that comes to you: in the dry season everything in the park is at one of the waterholes.
namibia/safari.alt: elephants and zebra at an Etosha waterhole, Namibia

namibia/wildlife.caption: Desert-Adapted Wildlife
namibia/wildlife.description: Elephant and rhino that walk sixty kilometres between water, and lion that hunt seals.
namibia/wildlife.alt: a desert-adapted elephant in a dry riverbed, Namibia

uganda/adventure.caption: Grade Five on the Nile
uganda/adventure.description: White-water rafting below the source at Jinja, plus bungee, kayaking and the long walk up Sipi.
uganda/adventure.alt: white-water rafting on the Nile rapids at Jinja, Uganda

uganda/architecture.caption: Minaret, Dome and Thatch
uganda/architecture.description: The Uganda National Mosque, the Namirembe and Rubaga cathedrals facing each other across two hills.
uganda/architecture.alt: the minaret of the Uganda National Mosque above Kampala

uganda/beaches.caption: The Ssese Islands
uganda/beaches.description: Freshwater beaches and fishing villages on Lake Victoria, an hour and a half by ferry from Entebbe.
uganda/beaches.alt: a sandy freshwater shore and fishing boats on the Ssese Islands, Uganda

uganda/cities.caption: Kampala on Seven Hills
uganda/cities.description: A capital built across hills and traffic, with the Gaddafi Mosque minaret giving the best view of all of it.
uganda/cities.alt: the hills and rooftops of Kampala seen from the Gaddafi Mosque minaret, Uganda

uganda/crafts.caption: Bark Cloth and Basketry
uganda/crafts.description: Bark cloth from the mutuba fig, made in Buganda for six hundred years and now UNESCO-listed.
uganda/crafts.alt: a craftsman beating bark cloth from a mutuba fig tree, Uganda

uganda/culture.caption: The Kingdom of Buganda
uganda/culture.description: Uganda's kingdoms were never abolished for long — Buganda, Bunyoro and Toro still hold court.
uganda/culture.alt: a Buganda kingdom drummer in ceremonial bark cloth

uganda/eco-tourism.caption: The Gorilla Permit
uganda/eco-tourism.description: Permit revenue funds the park and pays a share to the parishes around it — which is why the gorilla numbers are rising.
uganda/eco-tourism.alt: rangers and trackers setting out on a gorilla trek in Bwindi, Uganda

uganda/family-community.caption: Villages at the Forest Edge
uganda/family-community.description: Community walks in Buhoma and Nkuringo, run by the villages that share the forest with the gorillas.
uganda/family-community.alt: a community village walk beside the forest edge at Buhoma, Uganda

uganda/festivals.caption: Imbalu and Nyege Nyege
uganda/festivals.description: The Bagisu Imbalu season in the east, and four days of music on the banks of the Nile at Jinja.
uganda/festivals.alt: drummers and dancers at the Imbalu ceremony in eastern Uganda

uganda/food.caption: Rolex, Matoke, Luwombo
uganda/food.description: Steamed green banana with groundnut sauce, chicken cooked in banana leaf, and an egg rolled in a chapati on every corner.
uganda/food.alt: a street vendor cooking rolex chapati and eggs in Kampala, Uganda

uganda/forests.caption: Kibale and Bwindi
uganda/forests.description: Thirteen primate species in Kibale, and in Bwindi a forest so old and so thick it was never logged.
uganda/forests.alt: dense canopy and buttressed trees in Kibale Forest, Uganda

uganda/heritage.caption: Kingdoms Still Standing
uganda/heritage.description: Royal drums, regalia and clan structures that survived the protectorate, the 1966 crisis and the 1970s.
uganda/heritage.alt: royal regalia and drums inside a Buganda kingdom palace

uganda/hero.caption: The Pearl of Africa
uganda/hero.description: Gorilla forest, the Mountains of the Moon and the Nile leaving Lake Victoria — all inside one small, green country.
uganda/hero.alt: mist over the forested hills of Bwindi Impenetrable National Park at sunrise, Uganda

uganda/hidden-gems.caption: Kidepo Valley
uganda/hidden-gems.description: The furthest park from Kampala and the emptiest: Narus valley, the Morungole range, and cheetah nobody photographs.
uganda/hidden-gems.alt: the Narus valley and mountains of Kidepo Valley National Park, Uganda

uganda/historic-sites.caption: The Kasubi Tombs
uganda/historic-sites.description: The burial ground of four Buganda kings, thatched, enormous and rebuilt by the clans who have always maintained it.
uganda/historic-sites.alt: the great thatched dome of the Kasubi Tombs in Kampala, Uganda

uganda/lakes-rivers.caption: Where the Nile Begins
uganda/lakes-rivers.description: The Nile leaves Lake Victoria at Jinja; Lake Bunyonyi holds twenty-nine islands and no bilharzia.
uganda/lakes-rivers.alt: the islands and terraced shores of Lake Bunyonyi, Uganda

uganda/local-life.caption: Boda Bodas and Owino
uganda/local-life.description: The boda boda is the transport system; Owino market is where the whole city goes to buy everything.
uganda/local-life.alt: boda boda motorcycle taxis waiting at a busy Kampala street stage, Uganda

uganda/luxury.caption: Lodges at the Forest Edge
uganda/luxury.description: Small lodges on the Bwindi ridge and the Kazinga Channel, close enough to walk to the trailhead after breakfast.
uganda/luxury.alt: a lodge terrace overlooking the Bwindi forest ridge at dawn, Uganda

uganda/mountains.caption: The Mountains of the Moon
uganda/mountains.description: The Rwenzori range holds glaciers three degrees from the equator, and Margherita Peak at 5,109 m.
uganda/mountains.alt: the glaciated peaks of the Rwenzori Mountains above the moorland, Uganda

uganda/nature.caption: Green, End to End
uganda/nature.description: Crater lakes around Fort Portal, papyrus swamp on the Nile, and the Rwenzori snowline sitting on the equator.
uganda/nature.alt: the crater lakes and green hills around Fort Portal, Uganda

uganda/outdoor.caption: Sipi, Elgon, Bisoke
uganda/outdoor.description: Three waterfalls and a coffee walk at Sipi, then the long crater rim of Mount Elgon above it.
uganda/outdoor.alt: the Sipi Falls dropping off the Mount Elgon escarpment, Uganda

uganda/photography.caption: Crater Lakes at First Light
uganda/photography.description: The Ndali-Kasenda crater field before the haze lifts, and the Ishasha fig trees in the late afternoon.
uganda/photography.alt: morning mist on the Ndali-Kasenda crater lakes near Fort Portal, Uganda

uganda/safari.caption: Queen Elizabeth and Kidepo
uganda/safari.description: Kob on the Kasenyi plains, elephant on the Kazinga Channel, and Kidepo Valley with almost nobody in it.
uganda/safari.alt: elephants on the Kazinga Channel in Queen Elizabeth National Park, Uganda

uganda/traditional-people.caption: Batwa and Karamojong
uganda/traditional-people.description: The Batwa, forest people of the southwest, and the Karamojong cattle-keepers of the northeast plains.
uganda/traditional-people.alt: a Karamojong herder with cattle on the plains of Karamoja, Uganda

uganda/waterfalls.caption: Murchison, Through the Gap
uganda/waterfalls.description: The entire Victoria Nile forced through a seven-metre gap and dropped forty-three metres into the gorge below.
uganda/waterfalls.alt: the Nile forcing through the narrow gap at Murchison Falls, Uganda

uganda/why-visit.caption: Half the World's Gorillas
uganda/why-visit.description: Nowhere else puts gorillas, chimpanzees, the Big Five, a snowline and the Nile within one week of driving.
uganda/why-visit.alt: a silverback mountain gorilla resting in the Bwindi undergrowth, Uganda

uganda/wildlife.caption: Wildlife Encounters
uganda/wildlife.description: Mountain gorillas in Bwindi, chimpanzees in Kibale, and tree-climbing lions in the Ishasha sector.
uganda/wildlife.alt: a mountain gorilla in the Bwindi Impenetrable Forest, Uganda
